tools.description:
Summarise what a dataset holds: file types, folders, and how much is annotated.

Answers "what kind of files are in here" without running any model, so it costs nothing
and mutates nothing. Feed the result to a caller that can write prose — this returns
facts, not a narrative.

The platform offers no aggregation API, so counts come from a bounded client-side scan.
Check `scan_truncated`: above the cap the numbers are proportions of a sample, not a
census of the dataset, and must be described that way.

max_scan.description: Cap on items inspected. Counts are a sample above this.

sample.description: How many example filenames to include.

tools.description:
Run an installed model over items so its predictions land as annotations.

Use this to learn what is actually *in* a dataset when filenames and labels do not say.

Two consequences to state before confirming. Inference is **billable**, per item over a
whole dataset. And predictions are **written onto the items as annotations**, so a dataset
someone only wanted to explore comes back changed; `annotation_delete_by_model` undoes
exactly this model's contribution.

confirm.description: Must be true: inference is billable and writes annotations.

dataset_id.description: Run over an entire dataset. Cost scales with its item count.

item_ids.description: Items to run over. Provide this or dataset_id, not both.

model_id.description: An installed, deployed model; model_list shows status.

tools.description:
Define which of a model's dataset items it trains or validates on.

Without this, training draws on whatever the dataset holds — including items whose
annotations nobody has reviewed, and items a PII scan flagged. Filtering on a review
marker written through `item_update` is what makes a review step actually bind;
`exclude_pii` is what keeps flagged data out of a training run.

PiiMarkerSpec.description: How a PII scan records its verdict on an item. Caller-supplied; exactly one shape required.

annotation_label.description: Annotation label carried when PII is found, e.g. 'pii'.

entity_types.description: Entity types counting as PII, e.g. ['US_SSN', 'CREDIT_CARD']. Matches metadata.user.pii — the shape this server's own writeback produces.

metadata_field.description: User metadata field another scanner sets, e.g. 'pii_detected'.

metadata_value.description: Value that field takes when found. Default true.

annotated_only.description: Restrict to items that carry annotations.

directory.description: Restrict to items under this folder.

exclude_pii.description: Exclude items a PII scan flagged. Same marker shape as pii_report.

metadata_field.description: Only items whose user metadata carries this field, e.g. 'reviewed'.

metadata_value.description: Required value for metadata_field. Defaults to true.

tools.description:
Answer "does this dataset contain PII?" for a dataset a PII scan has already run over.

Reports how many items carry the marker, out of how many, with a sample. A zero count
means *no item carries the marker* — which is not the same as "no PII is present" if the
scan never ran or the marker convention is wrong, so the response states both counts and
the exact filter used, for the caller to sanity-check.

PiiMarkerSpec.description: How a PII scan records its verdict on an item. Caller-supplied; exactly one shape required.

annotation_label.description: Annotation label carried when PII is found, e.g. 'pii'.

entity_types.description: Entity types counting as PII, e.g. ['US_SSN', 'CREDIT_CARD']. Matches metadata.user.pii — the shape this server's own writeback produces.

metadata_field.description: User metadata field another scanner sets, e.g. 'pii_detected'.

metadata_value.description: Value that field takes when found. Default true.

marker.description: How a PII finding is recorded — an annotation label or a metadata field.

sample.description: How many flagged items to show.

tools.name: pii_report
tools.title: Report PII findings in a dataset

tools.description:
Write which kinds of PII were found to the source item's `metadata.user.pii`.

The map holds detected entity types only — `{"US_SSN": true}` — never counts, scores, or
matched values. An undetected type is absent rather than false, so a query is always
"<TYPE> is true", which negates cleanly and gives a dependable exclusion.

An item scanned with nothing found gets an empty map. That empty map is the only record
that the scan ran, so do not strip it.

PiiFindingsSpec.description:
What a PII scan found on one item.

Written to `metadata.user.pii` as a flat map of detected entity type to `true` — e.g.
``{"US_SSN": true, "EMAIL_ADDRESS": true}``. Nothing else goes in that map: no counts, no
scores, and above all none of the matched strings. The map answers "which kinds of PII are
in here", which is what routing and exclusion need; the values themselves are the PII, and
copying them into metadata would put them somewhere more queryable and more exportable than
the document they came from.

An entity type that was not detected is **absent**, not `false`. The map's presence is what
records that a scan ran, so a scanned-clean item carries an empty map.

entity_types.description: Entity types detected on this item, e.g. ['US_SSN', 'EMAIL_ADDRESS']. Each becomes a `<TYPE>: true` pair. Empty means scanned and nothing found.

findings.description: Entity types detected. Each becomes a `<TYPE>: true` pair.

item_id.description: Source item to record findings on.

tools.name: pii_set_findings
tools.title: Record PII findings on an item

tools.description:
Add a code node that turns each PDF into a text item.

Extracts with pypdf on DOE, uploads to `/rag/text` tagged with the source id, and
returns that item. A PDF yielding no text fails the execution.

output_dataset_id.description: Dataset the text item is written to.

pipeline_id.description: Pipeline to add the node to.

tools.title: Add PDF-to-text conversion node

tools.description:
Add a code node that splits a text item into overlapping chunk items.

Each chunk is an item under `/rag/chunks`, tagged with its source and offsets: a
feature vector attaches to an entity, so chunk-level retrieval needs chunk items.

output_dataset_id.description: Dataset the chunk items go to.

pipeline_id.description: Pipeline to add the node to.

tools.title: Add text-to-chunks node

tools.description:
Add a code node that embeds a document's chunk items with a deployed model.

The model service writes each vector into its own feature set; nothing goes into item
metadata. Billable, and the model must already be deployed.

pipeline_id.description: Pipeline to add the node to.

tools.name: rag_add_embedding_node
tools.title: Add embedding generation node

tools.description:

The code nodes upload the items themselves; this is where further automation hangs.

pipeline_id.description: Pipeline to add the node to.

tools.name: rag_add_output_node
tools.title: Add output storage node

tools.description:
Rank chunk items against a query by vector similarity over the feature set.

The query is embedded by the same model as the chunks — uploaded as a throwaway item,
embedded, read back, deleted. Ranking is local (`dtlpy` has no vector-distance query)
over a bounded sample: check `scan_truncated`.

feature_set_id.description: Feature set to search. Defaults to the model's, or the only one.

model_id.description: The model that embedded the chunks; another's vectors do not compare.
